property_summary: If caller is marked admin, calling newEmergencyOracle must deploy an EmergencyOracle whose owner() equals the caller and whose description matches the input string; non-admin calls must revert.
Calling newEmergencyOracle either reverts (when caller is not an admin) or succeeds without changing C.isAdmin(address(this)) (the admin mapping for the caller does not become false as a result).
Calling newEmergencyOracle either reverts, or if it succeeds the deployed EmergencyOracle's description matches the input string and the caller (msg.sender) remains an admin in C.
Calling newEmergencyOracle never makes C.isAdmin(address(this)) become true if it was false before (i.e., the call cannot grant admin rights to the caller).
Calling newEmergencyOracle never revokes the caller's admin status: if caller is admin before the call then it remains admin afterwards (even if the call reverts or succeeds).
If caller is admin, newEmergencyOracle must deploy an EmergencyOracle whose owner is the caller and emit NewEmergencyOracle; otherwise the call must revert and no NewEmergencyOracle is emitted.

Calling newEmergencyOracle either reverts (when caller is not admin) or succeeds and increases C's reported isAdmin mapping for the same address remains unchanged (i.e., call does not flip isAdmin[msg.sender]).

Calling newEmergencyOracle by an admin must either revert or emit NewEmergencyOracle and not change isAdmin[address(this)] (i.e., the call cannot flip the caller's admin status), and when it succeeds the returned new oracle address (from the event) must not be zero.
Calling newEmergencyOracle never changes C.isAdmin(address(this)); the caller's admin flag remains the same regardless of success or revert.
Calling newEmergencyOracle never changes C.address(this).balance (the contract's Ether balance) regardless of success or revert.

When an admin calls newEmergencyOracle(description), it must either revert (if caller isn't admin) or emit NewEmergencyOracle and create an EmergencyOracle whose owner equals the caller and whose description matches the provided string (observable by checking that the emitted new oracle address is non-zero and that calling owner() on it returns the caller).
